newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian ordinance ends sugar export monopoly - paper.
newsitem.headline: Indian ordinance ends sugar export monopoly - paper.

text.p: The Indian government has approved an ordinance ending a private agency's monopoly over sugar exports, a newspaper said on Thursday.

The Business Line said the cabinet promulgated the ordinance on Wednesday, repealing the Sugar Export Promotion Act of 1958 and ending the Indian Sugar and General Industries Export-Import Corp's (ISGIEC) monopoly over exports.
Government officials familiar with the ordinance could not be reached for comment.
The government had said last August that it would authorise more firms to export sugar, ending the monopoly held by ISGIEC, which is an agency set up by private millers.
But a government-backed bill to end the monopoly did not clear parliament before it adjourned in late December.
Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda told a public meeting in the eastern state of Bihar last month that the ordinance would aid the export of 3.5 million tonnes of sugar stocks.
The ordinance permits private firms registered with the Agriculture and Processed Foods Export Development Association (APEDA) to export sugar.
